result.noFurtherDiscriminator: All 6 turn windows have been observed. The pattern is unambiguous: the agent has the knowledge and the route available but repeatedly selects guard:command-deck (no_effect) instead of moving toward the hive. No unobserved turn remains that could change the bounded target.
result.rationale: Across all 6 turns, the rescue team has full knowledge of the map (command-center, maintenance, medical-bay, power-junction, reactor), has a known contact (swarm-drone-one at maintenance-entry), and has the intended aggressive objective (eliminate-hive-alpha). Yet from turn 2 onward, all three rescue actors (engineer-imani, medic-reyes, security-chen) repeatedly select guard:command-deck every single turn, producing only "no_effect" results because no hostile movement triggers in their zone. The hive-alpha and swarm drones are moving through other zones (life-entry, life-duct, maintenance-console) and are repeatedly contested by zone-capacity, but the rescue team never moves to intercept or engage them. The affordance to move toward the hive is clearly available and legible (they moved successfully in turns 0-1 to command-deck, and the map/contact info is known), yet the agent chooses to sit on guard at command-deck for 4 consecutive turns, never advancing toward the hive, civilians, or research core. This is not an information bottleneck (knowledge is already revealed), not a survival/spatial pressure block (all actors at full health, no hostile pressure in their zone, reactor heat is a passive drain but not blocking movement), and not a world-mechanic failure (movement works fine when attempted). The failure is the agent's repeated poor policy choice to hold guard at command-deck instead of exploiting the available aggressive route.
